situation:
You are the marketing director at CRESTLINE SPORTS PROPERTIES, the co-operative that runs ticketing, sponsorship and marketing for the HARLAN STATE UNIVERSITY athletics department. The fifteen people who work at CRESTLINE own it in equal shares. The managing member (judge) has asked you to recommend what the coming season's marketing plan should be built around.

The plan on the table is built around the university's best-known basketball player. His photograph is on the renewal mailing, on the arena banners and across the department's social accounts, and renewals moved earlier last year than in any season before it. That campaign has already been designed and paid for, and renewals open in three weeks.

Last month the player signed a paid endorsement with a sports-betting application and began posting its promotions to his personal accounts. State law allows it, conference rules allow it, and the university's own policy allows it. He has not been asked to stop, and under the rules as they stand he cannot be required to.

Season-ticket holders have written in anyway. Many of them buy family packages, and the department's published statement of what it stands for says it markets to families first. The department could rebuild the campaign around the team and the student section, which would answer those letters, but it discards work already bought weeks before renewals open and singles out one player for conduct the rules permit, which his teammates would notice.

It can also keep the player at the center, which holds the renewal momentum and costs it the families who have already objected. The managing member (judge) wants you to select the target market this plan should serve, explain how the department's core values and position carry through it, and say where a player's personal posting ends and the department's business accounts begin. The managing member (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the managing member (judge) at CRESTLINE SPORTS PROPERTIES. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You were elected to the role by the same fifteen owner-employees whose livelihoods ride on the coming season, and this plan is the largest thing they will vote on. You want to hear which target market the plan should serve, how the core values and the position of the department would carry through it, and where the line sits between a player's personal posting and the accounts the department runs as a business.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would show us we got it wrong?
